header:
Date: 2025-10-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ivy Chen (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Lena Morales (Quantaco Head of ML), Omar Rizvi (Quantaco SRE), Priya Das (Quantaco Product), Ethan Wu (Quantaco ML Engineer)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/poc/quantaco/cost-calc.xlsx, https://redwood.ai/poc/quantaco/benchmark-logs
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Reviewed current tokens/sec/$ numbers, KV/prefix caching savings, batching tradeoffs and latency impact. Agreed to run additional benchmarks with prefix caching enabled and quantized model, update cost calc and align on production QPS and SLOs.
topics: tokens per second per dollar (tokens/sec/$) baseline
KV/prefix caching impact and hit-rate assumptions
Routing and fallback to hosted variants
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is the weekly POC sync focused on cost econ. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Lena Morales: Hi Lena here.
[00:12] Omar Rizvi: Omar, SRE.
[00:15] Priya Das: Priya.
[00:17] Ethan Wu: Ethan.
[00:19] Ivy Chen: Ivy from Redwood, hey.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Cool. Marcus is on but might drop in later. Agenda: quick recap of last weeks runs, tokens/sec/$ numbers, caching assumptions, then decide bench steps.
[00:35] Lena Morales: Sounds good. I did want to say the product team is sensitive to p95 latency above 400ms for chat, but for async batch embeddings we care more about cost.
[00:45] Samir Patel: Right, noted. For the baseline run last week - we measured ~18k tokens/sec on the c5-like instance with the standard open model, which translated to about 0.42 tokens/sec/$ in our hosted price calc, but that didn't include any cache.
[01:05] Ethan Wu: Quick clarification, is that tokens per second per dollar at peak or averaged? Our traffic spikes and we care about tail.
[01:12] Ivy Chen: That was average steady-state. Peak throughput hit 25k t/s in short bursts. Tail latency at p95 was around 320ms without caching.
[01:25] Priya Das: And what's the assumed cost unit? GPU minutes or instance per hour?
[01:29] Samir Patel: Good point - spreadsheet uses $/GPU-hour equivalent for Dedicated pricing and converted to tokens/sec/$ by throughput observed. I'll send the updated sheet with both hosted and dedicated assumptions.
[01:40] Omar Rizvi: For us, the question is how much caching can reduce token work. If you can reuse KV cache across similar prompts, that could be a big win.
[01:50] Ivy Chen: Exactly - our prefix/KV cache on similar conversation flows gave us ~45% token savings in the test harness last month. But the effective savings depend on hit-rate; we modeled 30/50/70% hit-rate scenarios in the calc.
[02:05] Lena Morales: Is that 45% end-to-end or just decoding cost? Because we have long prompts sometimes.
[02:11] Ivy Chen: Mostly decoding, so end-to-end token bill reduces but you still pay some prefix processing depending on where the cache sits - if it's full KV cache, you can avoid recomputing initial layers. There's room for variation.
[02:25] Samir Patel: In numbers: baseline tokens/sec/$ 0.42. With a conservative 30% cache hit, effective tokens/sec/$ moves to about 0.60. With 50% hit it's ~0.83. With aggressive 70% it's over 1.1 tokens/sec/$. Those are roughs but we can share exact calc.
[02:45] Ethan Wu: Nice. For latency impact though, does caching reduce p95?
[02:50] Ivy Chen: It can reduce end-to-end latency for subsequent queries since KV reuse avoids generating prefix tokens, so p95 drops - we saw p95 drop from 320ms to ~210ms in sample flows. But there's a tradeoff: caching lookups and serialization for large caches can add overhead at scale; depends on implementation and network locality.
[03:10] Omar Rizvi: If cache is remote across a network hop it might add 10-20ms, which still nets positive. But we need to ensure consistent hit-rate.
[03:18] Samir Patel: On batching: we tested batch sizes 1, 4, 8. Batch 4 gave best tokens/sec/$ improvement (roughly 1.6x vs batch 1) but increased median latency by ~70ms for single queries. If most of your workload is concurrent small chats, batching helps throughput and cost but can hurt single-user latency.
[03:40] Priya Das: Our mix is 60% interactive chat (low latency required) and 40% background scoring. So sounds like a mixed routing policy might be needed.
[03:49] Ivy Chen: Redwood can route interactive traffic to a low-batch, low-latency pool and background scoring to a high-throughput pool with aggressive batching and caching. That way cost is optimized without violating p95 for the chat users.
[04:05] Lena Morales: What about quantization - can we push a 4-bit model? We worry about quality regressions for some intents.
[04:12] Ivy Chen: We support INT8/4-bit quantized variants. In our evals, 4-bit sometimes has slight regressions on few-shot reasoning tests. Our recommendation is to validate on your sample prompts - we can run a quality regression test set against the quantized model.
[04:30] Ethan Wu: Could do that. If quality drop is acceptable on non-critical intents we can use quantized models for scoring and full precision for chat.
[04:38] Samir Patel: Good. So immediate bench steps - Ivy will run a dedicated 1hr batch with prefix caching enabled at three hit-rate sims and quantized model, capture tokens/sec, p50/p95 and cost numbers. Samir will fold that into spreadsheet and present tokens/sec/$ under hosted vs dedicated pricing.
[04:58] Omar Rizvi: We'll share our expected peak QPS and SLA numbers - currently target p95 < 400ms for chat and 99.9% uptime.
[05:06] Priya Das: Also please include regression alerts and eval hooks in the plan - product needs automated quality checks if we change quant or model.
[05:12] Ivy Chen: Yes we can wire in eval runs and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We have the Redwood Optimize hooks for that.
[05:20] Lena Morales: Any blockers on compliance or data residency for these bench runs?
[05:24] Samir Patel: For the POC data we're fine with hosted, but for production we heard you might need private deployment in EU region - we'll factor that into costs once you confirm.
[05:34] Lena Morales: Correct, production must be EU region and KMS integration. That could change the cost numbers slightly.
[05:40] Samir Patel: Noted - I'll add a column for EU private pricing in the sheet.
[05:44] Marcus Lee: (joining) Sorry - quick note: we'll also instrument token-level cost breakdown in the Redwood Console so you can see per-route and per-user cost.
[05:52] Ethan Wu: That would be super helpful to debug hotspots.
[05:55] Samir Patel: Alright looks like we're aligned. Any final questions?
[06:00] Priya Das: One ask - can you include an example of routing policy config for mixed workloads? We want a template.
[06:07] Ivy Chen: Yes we'll send a sample policy with canary and fallback to hosted variant if dedicated capacity is exhausted.
[06:14] Samir Patel: Great. Recap of action items: Samir update cost calc, Ivy run benchmarks, Omar provide SLO/QPS, Priya confirm acceptance criteria. We'll meet again same time next week.
[06:28] Lena Morales: Thanks everyone.
[06:30] (call ends)
